newsitem.title: FRANCE: Santer says EU farm price cuts will boost exports.
newsitem.headline: Santer says EU farm price cuts will boost exports.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Wednesday that proposals to cut farm support prices towards world levels will help European farmers, notably grain and beef producers, to increase exports.
Dairy, cereals and beef intervention prices would be cut by 10, 20 and 30 percent respectively by 2006 under plans to prepare for EU expansion eastwards.
"It will also put the EU in a strong position for the next round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) negotiations," he told the European Parliament while presenting the so-called Agenda 2000.
WTO talks on further cuts in farm subsidies are due to start in 1999.
Santer said lower intervention prices would ease the integration of eastern European countries, whose prices were generally much lower.

"It would also reduce the risk of uncontrolled growth in production in the future member states," he said, adding that alarmist forecasts of an explosion in EU farm spending were absolutely unfounded.
The EU has proposed opening talks with Hungary, Poland, the Czech republic, Slovenia and Estonia -- the first wave of 10 prospective eastern European members.
Santer warned that the EU could not continue to over-compensate farmers for income losses due to cuts in intervention prices.
"That's why the Commission envisages compensation of less than 100 percent," he said, adding that world market prices were expected to remain above EU intervention levels.
The Commission has estimated that cereals farmers were paid 8.5 billion Ecus too much over the past four years for income losses that were expected after 1992 farm reform price cuts.
